artworks.title: Neptune and Amymone
artworks.description: Metropolitan Museum print of Neptune/Poseidon with Amymone — the Danaid he rescues from a satyr and rewards with the Lernaean spring, mother of Nauplius.

artworks.title: Amymone Rescued by Poseidon
artworks.description: Bunny's Symbolist canvas: Poseidon lifts Amymone from the satyr's pursuit — Danaus' daughter as modern mythic nude, the Argive spring-myth restaged in oil.

artworks.title: Amymone
artworks.description: Mocetto's engraving isolates Amymone — the Danaid of the Poseidon encounter, Venetian print culture's face for the Lernaean bride.

artworks.title: Poseidon and Amymone (Paphos mosaic)
artworks.description: House of Dionysus, Paphos: Poseidon and Amymone in tesserae — the Cypriot floor that fixed the Danaid's sea-god rescue for late antiquity.

artworks.title: Amymone (Aison Painter oinochoe)
artworks.description: Kerameikos oinochoe: Amymone among satyrs — Attic red-figure of the Danaid before Poseidon's rescue, hydria in hand for her father's water-quest.

popCulture.title: Amymone
popCulture.description: Danaid daughter of Danaus; by Poseidon mother of Nauplius — not every butterfly that borrowed her name.

popCulture.title: Danaus
popCulture.description: Amymone's father — the Egyptian exile who arms his fifty daughters for the wedding night in Argos.
